subject: fine-arts
general_outcomes: By the end of senior school, the learner should be able to;
Deepen visual perception skills through exploration of various artistic techniques in 2Dimensional and 3Dimensional works.
Promote understanding of diverse fine art works from Kenya to promote patriotism.
Demonstrate appreciation of the Fine art through the historical perspective
Acquire research and analytical skills to document and critique artworks.
Explore a range of materials, techniques and tools used in fine arts to create functional and aesthetic artworks.
Explore and develop skills in ICT for design, production and presentation of fine artworks.
Apply creative and innovative skills to make materials from upcycled and recycled objects from the immediate environment.
Demonstrate understanding of the creative process in fine arts for portfolio development. (documen
Acquire art related entrepreneurial skills for economic empowerment.
Appreciate indigenous African crafts and use them as sources of inspiration in design and production.

substrands.name: Pottery and Ceramics
learning_outcomes: analyse properties of clay in pottery
prepare clay for pottery
model a hand-built vase using the pellet technique
fire the pellet vases in an updraught kiln
appraise the hand-built pellet vases for feedback.
learning_experiences: Learners are guided to:
research virtual and/actual sources on pottery focusing on; practise in Kenya, properties (plasticity, porosity, vitrification) and preparation of clay.
source clay,drying, crushing, slaking,sieving,drying, kneading and wedging; and store for use
watch a video on pellet technique to analyse uniformity and joining of pellets
model a clay vase using the pellet technique with emphasis on uniformity of pellets joinery of clay pellets considering elements and principles of 3D Art
collaboratively use recyclable materials to build an updraught kiln considering safety
fire the pellet vases in the updraught kiln observing safety precautions
display own and others’ work for peer feedback and reflection.
inquiry_questions: 1. How can you overcome the challenges in modeling using pellet technique?
2. What factors are considered when choosing a location for an updraught kiln?
core_competencies: Imagination and creativity: as the learner builds a vase using the pellet technique.
Digital literacy: as the learner uses ICT tools to explore pottery made using the pellet technique
Critical thinking and problem solving: as the learner chooses a site and builds an updraught kiln.
values: Responsibility: as the learner is guided to take good care of own and others’ pottery items to avoid breakage during drying and firing and when being guided to cautiously handle fire during the firing process to avoid fire accidents.
Patriotism: as the learner exhibits awareness of own responsibilities in the society by prudent use of clay and conserving the environment by protecting riparian land areas from over-exploitation
pertinent_issues: Health Education (Personal hygiene): as the learner is guided on the need to maintain high standards of personal and environmental cleanliness when working with clay.
Citizenship (Social cohesion): as the learner interacts amicably with others as they construct the updraught kiln.

substrands.name: Sculpture
learning_outcomes: examine the concept of relief sculpture for inspiration
carve a relief sculpture for skill acquisation
value own and others’ relief sculptural forms.
learning_experiences: Learners are guided to:

explore virtual and/or actual samples of indigenous relief sculptures in Eastern and central Africa (Makonde, Akamba, Karamajong’ and Bamileke of DRC) emphasis on; subject matter, material, tools and finishing techniques

design and carve a relief sculpture inspired by indigenous sculptures from East Africa, with emphasis on; -interpretation of subject matter -selection and preparation of appropriate recyclable material from the environment. -elements and principles of 3 D Art, -finishing
• communicate with clarity as they display and critique own and others artwork.
inquiry_questions: 1. How are the principles of 3D art portrayed in sculpture?
2. How can you experiment with organic and inorganic materials for a quality finish on relief sculptures?
core_competencies: Imagination and Creativity: as the learner designs and carve wooden masks in relief.

Self-efficacy: as the learner demonstrates persistence, commitment, and resilience during the production of the sculptural forms, exhibits self-esteem and confidence during critique of one's own and others’ art works.
values: Responsibility: as the learner is encouraged to recycle and upcycle materials in order to take care of the environment.
Patriotism: as the learner exhibits awareness of own responsibilities in the society by prudent use of materials (wood) and restoring the environment by planting trees.
pertinent_issues: Citizenship Education: learner is sensitized on appreciation of ethnic diversities when exploring relief sculptures from Eastern and Central African region.

Socio-Economic and Environmental Issues: Waste management as the learner is encouraged to recycle and upcycle organic and inorganic waste materials from the immediate environment to make relief sculptures for environmental conservation.

substrands.name: Weaving
learning_outcomes: examine the process of constructing a square knot for making a web
construct an ornamental wall hanging using square knots
analyze the process of constructing a spiral knot
construct a two colour bag using spiral knots
use open source software to design a wall hanging with a combination of square and spiral knots
appreciate own and others’ macrame artworks.
learning_experiences: Learners are guided to:
observe and discuss video clips on the process of making square knots focusing on loose knotting of the web and tight or compact knotting of the web
construct 2 colour webs using square knots embedded with recycled beads to make an ornamental wall hanging
Observe video clips and discuss the structure of a spiral knots
construct 2 colour webs using spiral knots embedded with recycled beads to make a bag
Use the Macrame’ mobile app to design a bag using a combination of square and spiral knots
Make the bag following the design.
• display and critique own and others’ works reflecting on the knotted bags.
inquiry_questions: 1. How can Macrame’ be used to make wall hangings?
2. How does choice of knots influence the appearance of Macrame’ item?
core_competencies: Critical thinking and problem solving: as the learner adapts technology to develop designs of articles to be made in macrame
Imagination and Creativity: as the learner designs macrame’ articles/projects
Digital literacy: as the learner uses ICT tools to explore and create patterns for weaving.
values: Integrity: as the learner utilizes resources sparingly and avoids conflict of interest during critique sessions.
Respect: as the learner is encouraged to be sensitive to others’ opinions during class discussion.
Love: as the learner is encouraged to share materials and tools as they weave the waist bags.
pertinent_issues: Environmental conservation/ Global citizenship (sustainable development). -as the learner is guided on the need to conserve the environment as a source of art materials for weaving. -as learners are guided to reuse and recycle materials for weaving the waist bags.
Financial literacy: as the learner explores career opportunities in Multimedia Crafts through clubs, creates woven waist bags and learns marketing strategies.
Consumer Literacy: as the learner sources for safe and appropriate materials for use in weaving the waist bag.

substrands.name: Jewellery and Ornamentation
learning_outcomes: analyze materials and tools used in jewellery and ornamentation
produce a beaded cardholder using found objects
Make a necklace with a pendant
create a suncatcher bracelet for skill development
Appreciate own and others’ mixed media artworks.
learning_experiences: Learners are guided to:

Study and discuss actual and/or virtual samples of jewellery and ornamented items for inspiration with focus on; materials and tools used, techniques and processes, subject matter, function (adornment and decorating spaces).
explore the environment, collect and prepare materials for making the cardholder , NB: Learners to consider hygiene and safety precautions
design and make a functional cardholder with focus on; -varied materials -combination of sticking, plaiting, thonging, stitching and beadwork techniques. -principles of Art and Design (Balance
dominance, Rhythm and movement).
Safety measures when using sharp tools
make a necklace with a pendant using recycled materials while observing the following
Elements(colour, shape) and Principles (Balance, dominance, rhythm and movement)
Process (Preparing materials, carving/shaping the pendant, stringing, Finishing)
design and make a suncatcher bracelet using reflective materials among others with emphasis on
Elements(colour, shape, texture) and Principles(Balance, dominance, rhythm and movement).
Craftsmanship (experiments using the skills of; stitching
gluing, cutting, bending, twisting, piercing,threading/stringing,hole punching, painting, polishing.) observe safety measures
appreciate others’ diverse opinions and value human dignity during display and critique.
inquiry_questions: 1. How does jewellery and ornamentation contribute to environmental conservation?
2. How can the immediate environment provide inspiration for jewellery and ornamentation?
core_competencies: Critical thinking and problem solving: as the learner explores the environment, collects and prepares materials for leatherwork and jewellery while producing various functional and decorative items.
Experiments with different materials and techniques while making a suncatcher bracelet.

Communication as the learer; -seeks information and offers support while sourcing, preparing, using materials and sharing what they have learnt with others. -pays attention to the person speaking, takes turns in conversation during critique of own and others’ Mixed Media artworks.
Collaboration: as the learner amicably works together with peers, appreciates efforts of others while sourcing materials for leatherwork and jewellery.
values: Values:

Respect: as the learner appreciates diverse opinions and values human dignity during critique sessions. Social justice: as learners appreciate boundaries and permission while sourcing and preparing materials for jewellery and ornaments
pertinent_issues: Health promotion issues: as the learner is sensitized on the need to consider hygiene when collecting and cleaning found objects
Social economic and environmental issues: as the learner observes safety measures when using sharp tools used in leatherwork and jewellery.

substrands.name: Art Appreciation
learning_outcomes: analyze legal issues in production and marketing of artwork
formulate strategies of marketing artworks online
appreciate strategies of online marketing of artworks.
learning_experiences: Learners are guided to:
Actively participate in research and discussion on legal issues with regard to:
production of artwork (quality and safety of materials used)
marketing of artworks(misleading information,counterfeit)

Use digital devices to conduct research and prepare slides on; -the importance of marketing artworks online, -ways of marketing online,( organizing virtual art exhibition in social media forums, listing costed artworks in online market places, -advantages and disadvantages of online marketing)
Respect others opinions as they present and discuss the slides in class.
Suggested Assessment Methods
inquiry_questions: 1. Why is it important for practicing artists to know legal issues affecting the production of artwork?
2. How can one uphold integrity when marketing artworks?
Non-Formal Activities
